title: Keyword Flags
statement: Implement `solve(bound)`. `bound` is a dict of the names a call actually bound: it always contains `verbose` and `dry_run`, each 0 or 1, and it contains `label` only when the caller passed it. Return `{"verbose": ..., "dry_run": ..., "label": ...}`. The label is the string `none` when it was omitted. This is the shape of a function that forces flags to be keyword-only: the mapping is the bound arguments, not a positional pile.
constraints: verbose and dry_run are always present
A missing label key means the string none
hints: Use bound.get("label", "none") for the optional name.
Do not invent defaults other than none for the label.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: Keyword-only parameters stop a caller from passing a boolean in the wrong slot.

editorial: Keyword-only parameters stop a caller from passing a boolean in the wrong slot. After the call is bound, the function sees names, not positions. The omitted label is a missing key, reported as the token none so a test can see the difference between omitted and an empty label.
